chapterTitle: Unit 01: Nature of Science of Chemistry & Laboratory Safety
description: Introduction to chemistry, scientific inquiry, green chemistry principles, major branches (organic, inorganic, physical, analytical, biochemistry), and laboratory safety.
States of matter, physical/chemical properties, pure substances vs mixtures, homogeneous/heterogeneous mixtures, solutions, colloids, and suspensions.
Subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons), Thomson, Rutherford, and Bohr models, atomic number, mass number, isotopes, and electronic configuration (Aufbau principle).

chapterTitle: Unit 04: Periodic Table & Periodicity of Properties
description: Development of the periodic table, Mendeleev vs modern periodic law, groups and periods, periodic trends: atomic radius, ionic radius, ionization energy, electron affinity, and electronegativity.
Octet and duplet rules, chemical bonding types: ionic, covalent (single, double, triple, polar, non-polar), coordinate covalent, metallic bonding, and hydrogen bonding.
Atomic mass, molecular mass, formula mass, mole concept, Avogadro number, molar mass, empirical and molecular formulas, percentage composition, and stoichiometric calculations.
Oxidation and reduction concepts, oxidation states, balancing redox equations, electrolytic cells, galvanic (voltaic) cells, electroplating, and corrosion prevention.
Exothermic and endothermic reactions, thermochemical equations, enthalpy changes (ΔH), heat of reaction, activation energy, and energy diagrams.
Reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium, law of mass action, equilibrium constant (Kc), conditions of equilibrium, and Le Chatelier principle in chemical systems.
Arrhenius and Bronsted-Lowry theories of acids and bases, pH scale and indicators, neutralization reactions, preparation and properties of salts, and buffer concepts.

chapterTitle: Unit 11: Environmental Chemistry: Atmosphere & Air Pollution
description: Composition of atmosphere, troposphere and stratosphere, primary and secondary air pollutants (CO, SO2, NOx, VOCs), acid rain, greenhouse effect, and ozone layer depletion.

chapterTitle: Unit 12: Environmental Chemistry: Hydrosphere & Water Treatment
description: Occurrence and properties of water, soft and hard water, temporary and permanent hardness, methods of water softening, water pollution, and drinking water purification.

chapterTitle: Unit 13: Organic Chemistry: Carbon Chains & Functional Groups
description: Uniqueness of carbon (catenation, tetravalency), general formula and homologous series, IUPAC nomenclature, and identification of key functional groups (alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, ethers, carboxylic acids).
Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes), combustion, substitution and addition reactions, physical properties, and uses of methane, ethene, and ethyne.
Essential biomolecules: carbohydrates (monosaccharides, disaccharides, polysaccharides), proteins and amino acids, lipids and fatty acids, nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), vitamins, and dietary energy.

chapterTitle: Unit 16: Chemical Measurements, SI Units & Significant Figures
description: International System of Units (SI base and derived units), scientific notation, prefixes, measurement errors, precision vs accuracy, significant figures, and temperature scale conversions.
Separation of heterogeneous and homogeneous mixtures: filtration, crystallization, simple distillation, fractional distillation, solvent extraction, and sublimation.
Chemical industries: manufacture of ammonia by Haber process, sulfuric acid by Contact process, fertilizers (urea), cement, and environmental impact of industrial effluents.
Chromatographic separation techniques: paper chromatography, stationary and mobile phases, retention factor (Rf values), and introduction to instrumental analysis.
